newsitem.title: FINLAND: Yeltsin firm on NATO enlargement - Russian spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin firm on NATO enlargement - Russian spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin stood firm on opposition to NATO expansion in talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton but they moved closer to a deal on better ties between Moscow and the alliance, Russia said on Friday.

Asked if Yeltsin had altered his position on NATO plans to take in former Soviet bloc states at their first session of summit talks, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters: "He did not change it even in nuance."

"I have the impression that during these two hours the presidents not only advanced in understanding their respective positions but did more in that they actually moved towards each other in their positions," he said, referring to NATO's ties with Russia.
NATO is negotiating with Moscow on a charter which would forge a new relationship with Russia, giving it more of a say in European security without allowing it to veto alliance decisions.

Yastrzhembsky said there could be a joint statement from the presidents on European security after their summit talks end later on Friday. While Russia opposes NATO enlargement it has said it wants a good relations with the 16-nation alliance.
The Russian spokesman echoed the White House assessment of the first session of talks, saying the discussions were intense but not argumentative.
